compensating.why: hop 1 returns the list as it is
hop 2 hands hop 3 a copy of the node list
hop 3 inserts each block at the front of the result

context_edits.old: public void add(int index, Element element) {contents.add(index, element);}

ownership_reason: Only the gold decides which data nodes are kept and groups them into blocks: one pass over the node list that adds each data node to the current block and closes the block at a node of another kind. Hops 1, 2 and 4 pass the list along (making it unmodifiable, creating the result list), and hop 3 only concatenates the blocks the gold returns, in order. Once the gold leaves out the data nodes that end the list, they can reappear only if a caller re-reads the node list itself or replaces the gold. The gold's javadoc promises the blocks of the data nodes that follow one another, in document order, with only the nodes of other kinds left out; on the trigger input (a script element whose only child is a data node) the variant returns no block. The convention that every data-node child counts, the final one included, is pinned outside the gold: Element.data() appends the data of every DataNode child (HtmlParserTest handlesDataOnlyTags and handlesUnclosedScriptAtEof pass: a script or style whose only child is a data node gives its data), and the intact sibling filter Element.textNodes() keeps the text node that ends the child list (ElementTest testGetTextNodes passes with ' Four' as the third entry).
